Subject: BlueHarbor pilot — pricing & screening request

Team,

We're moving toward a pilot with BlueHarbor Logistics (procurement contact Ethan Dunn). Summary: 12-month pilot, estimated committed spend $420k ARR if they convert. They've asked for a 30% introductory discount and a clause allowing cross-border inference for US/EU nodes (customer operations across ports). Quote requires a non-standard export-control paragraph to permit limited cross-border inference and a 30% price concession for an initial 90-day pilot.

Immediate asks:
- Rishi: can you run an in-depth sanctions & end-use screen and confirm any red flags? I attached the initial customer W9 and SOW we provided.
- Laura: we need legal input on whether the proposed export clause is acceptable or whether a mitigated redline is required.
- Marissa: this is time-sensitive — customer expects contract this week. Can we escalate for an exec sign-off on the commercial exception (discount + clause) if compliance/legal OK?

Attachments: BlueHarbor_SOW_v2.pdf, BlueHarbor_W9.pdf

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-17T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BlueHarbor pilot — pricing & screening request

Karthik — thanks for the summary. Quick notes from a security/compliance perspective:

1) Initial automated sanctions scan returned a low-confidence match on an individual listed as a past contractor affiliated with a flagged overseas logistics intermediary. I exported the raw output (initial_sanctions_scan.csv) — needs manual review.
2) End-use: customer describes use of our model for routing/ETA predictions across shipments crossing EU/UK waters. That triggers data residency and controlled-technical-transfer considerations.

I need the following to proceed with a manual clearance:
- Completed KYC packet (company ownership, beneficial owners, admin contact, purpose of use)
- Clarification of data flows (which datasets will be sent to our hosted endpoints, any PII or export-controlled technical specs)
- Confirmation on whether BlueHarbor will request model weights/derivative artifacts (they said no but we need an explicit confirmation)

If BlueHarbor provides the KYC packet by EOD tomorrow I can aim to finish manual review within 48 hours. For now, I would not recommend signing any export-control carve-outs until manual review completes.

Rishi
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment referenced: initial_sanctions_scan.csv

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-18T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BlueHarbor pilot — pricing & screening request

Karthik / team — reviewed the requested language. Short answer: we can accept a limited export-control deviation but only with specific mitigations. Draft guidance below (high level):

- Replace a broad "cross-border inference" clause with a narrowly scoped paragraph that:
  * Permits inference only on customer-submitted data tagged as non-PII and non-controlled;
  * Requires processing to occur only in named regions (US primary, EU secondary) and expressly prohibits transfer of model weights or training data;
  * Requires BlueHarbor to warrant that its use-case is not for navigation systems classified under restricted controls (please confirm).

- For price concessions: any discount over 20% must be approved by Exec and recorded in our discounts ledger + SFDC. We should consider a staged concession: 25% for the first 60 days if compliance sign-off completed within 48 hours and an SLA/penalty clause for misuse.

I've prepared a redline: redline_export_clause.docx. Legal recommends we do not finalize until Rishi confirms no active sanctions/end-use red flags.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Markus — forwarding the thread and redlines. Short executive summary below:

- Customer: BlueHarbor Logistics (Ethan Dunn; procurement@blueharbor.com). Deal ID DH-2027-042; potential ARR if converted ~$420k.
- Ask: 30% introductory discount + permissive export-control clause to allow cross-border inference for specific non-PII routing/ETA workloads.
- Legal: will accept a narrow, mitigated clause (see attached redline) but recommends discount cap at 25% and staged concession tied to compliance completion.
- Security: preliminary sanctions scan flagged a low-confidence hit; Rishi needs a completed KYC packet to confirm clearance.
- Timeline: customer expects contract this week.

Recommendation (Marissa): conditional exec approval to offer a 25% pilot discount (not 30%) for 60 days, contingent on:
  1) Rishi signs off within 48 hours after receiving the KYC packet;
  2) Legal's redline export clause inserted verbatim;
  3) Revenue Ops logs discount and inserts an explicit end-date and rollback to standard pricing.

If you approve, please confirm and we'll route the redline to the customer and update the quote.

Marissa
VP Sales, Redwood Inference
